newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Kandir says will not stem demand.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Kandir says will not stem demand.

text.p: Brazilian Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said Thursday the government had no intentions of stemming consumer demand.
Kandir said he was not concerned with what is expected to be a record monthly trade gap in February.
"There is no intention of doing this (stemming consumption)," Kandir told reporters, adding that he did not think taking a short-term view of economic activity was beneficial.
The Finance Ministry Wednesday reviewed that Brazil had posted a $1.6 billion trade deficit in Jan 1 to Feb 23.
Kandir noted that were signs of reasonably high economic growth and said that this naturally led to an increase in imports.
But he said most of these imports contributed to Brazil's productivity, adding that high inflows of foreign capital and foreign direct investments were financing any shortfall in the current account.
